summary: In Homer's Catalogue of Ships, Gouneus (Ancient Greek: Γουνεύς; also Guneus) brings twenty-two ships from Cyphus, leading the Enienes (Aenianes) and the Perrhaebians who dwelt about wintry Dodona and the ploughland by the Titaressus. The fuller Returns tradition — survival and settlement near Libya's Cinyps — is carried on the companion atlas node guneus-aenian.

sections.heading: Homeric muster
paragraphs: According to Homer, "Guneus brought two and twenty ships from Cyphus, and he was followed by the Enienes and the valiant Peraebi, who dwelt about wintry Dodona" and the fair land by the Titaressus, which pours into the Peneius yet does not mix with that river's silver eddies (Iliad 2.748–755). The atlas keeps this Catalogue notice under the Homeric spelling Gouneus (gouneus-cyphus).

Homer does not record his pedigree. Elsewhere his parents are called Ocytus and Aurophyte (or Tauropoleia / Hippodameia); in a rare account his father is Cyphos, eponym of Cyphus. Apollodorus counts Guneus son of Ocytus among the captains of the Trojan muster.

sections.heading: Companion node
paragraphs: The same Catalogue captain's later fate — shipwreck at Caphereus and settlement near the Cinyps in Libya — is told on guneus-aenian, which also distinguishes him from Guneus of Pheneus, father of Laonome and grandfather of Amphitryon. Readers following the Homeric spelling land here first; the Returns and Pheneus homonym notes live on the Aenianian file.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (gouneus-cyphus) is the Homeric Cyphus captain. Same figure as guneus-aenian for the war and Libyan return; distinct from Guneus of Pheneus in Arcadia.
